mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened financing conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
regime_hint: Rising Fed Funds rate in late-cycle tightening
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during high-FED period (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not cross 4% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 5.5% predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as higher unemployment expectations depress equity risk premia.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) when UNRATE > 5.5%, or UNRATE does not cross threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real GDP) exceeds 2% growth over the prior quarter, S&P 20-day forward returns are positive as strong demand supports equity valuation expansion.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during high-GDPC1 growth quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 3% predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as weak supply signals economic weakness and lower growth expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or not statistically different from zero when INDPRO declines > 3%.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of CPIAUCSL > 2% inflation trigger a positive S&P 5-day forward return as markets anticipate rate cuts within the next quarter.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive or not significant when CPIAUCSL remains > 2% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in PAYEMS (employment) by over 100,000 in a month is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as labor market strength boosts sentiment.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative or not significant when PAYEMS increases by ≤ 100,000.

mechanism_narrative: A positive interaction between HOUST (housing starts) and FEDFUNDS (below 4%) predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as low rates and strong building activity signal economic recovery.
regime_hint: Recovery zone: low rates + rising housing
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not positive when both proxies show the interaction pattern.

mechanism_narrative: During a post-crisis expansion regime (UNRATE < 5% and FEDFUNDS < 4%), S&P 60-day forward returns are positive as markets anticipate sustained growth and stability.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not positive or regime condition not met.
